summary: Incomplete final choice emitted after connection flap when HTTP multiplexing resets keepalive
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that long-running SSE streams occasionally end with a partial last 'choice' payload (truncated last token and missing final end-marker) after transient network flaps. Impact: Upstream application treats the response as incomplete and retries generation, causing duplicate downstream actions and higher costs. Observed since 2026-02-25 during higher-than-normal CDN connection churn.

Environment details: Production, Dedicated deployment for ScribeHealth in us-east region. Customer uses HTTP/2 multiplexing via a third-party CDN that reuses connections aggressively and advertises short keepalive timeouts. Client is a browser-based dashboard using our JS SDK v0.9.2 connecting to the hosted SSE endpoint.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure client SDK to open SSE stream to /v1/generate with model redwood/gpt-2-medium and stream:true
2) Place traffic behind an HTTP/2 multiplexing CDN (simulate by setting short connection keepalive and forcing connection resets every ~30s),
3) Generate long outputs (~1200 tokens) so the connection remains open across keepalive resets,
4) Observe final chunk when the CDN resets the TCP/HTTP connection mid-stream: some sessions return a final 'choice' object missing trailing tokens and without a terminal 'end' event
logs: 2026-02-26T17:22:13Z [edge-proxy] conn-id=abcd1234: HTTP/2 RST_STREAM received, reason=GOAWAY; 2026-02-26T17:22:13Z [serving-runtime] request-id=req-7f9: stream closed while flushing tail buffer; last-flush-size=128 bytes; 2026-02-26T17:22:13Z [sdk-client] evt: 'partial-choice', tokens=... 'final_token_incomplete'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: connection-level reset at the edge caused chunk boundary to be dropped and our SSE framing code did not emit an explicit end marker when underlying transport aborted during tail-flush.
Reproduced locally by toggling HTTP/2 GOAWAY on nginx/traefik with multiplexing enabled; observed truncated last chunk consistently when GOAWAY occurred during final flush window.
Observed correlation with customer CDN aggressive keepalive (30s) + server-side flush interval (500ms) causing the final KV-cache flush to be in-flight when connection reset occurs.

Trace from serving-runtime shows 'stream_close_abrupt' path skipped end-event emission in ~40% of forced-reset reproductions. Root cause narrowed to edge reset combined with streaming flush path not resilient to RST_STREAM during chunk coalescing.
Cross-check: unrelated SSE resume logic (SUP-4721) handled reattachment but did not fix missing end-event when final fragment lost.
comments: 2026-02-26 - ScribeHealth (customer): We see the transcript end abruptly ~10% of sessions. App-side dedupe is working but we still see duplicated actions after retries. Happy to provide pcap and SDK logs.
2026-02-26 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks — we've escalated to infra eng. Can you share sdk logs and exact CDN config (keepalive, http2 settings)?

2026-02-27 - SRE (Liam Chen): Reproduced with simulated GOAWAY. Captured serving-runtime stack traces showing 'close during flush' path that doesn't push final 'end' marker to SSE wire. Adding instrumentation to count end-event emissions vs abrupt closes.

2026-02-28 - Eng (Marco Rivera): Patch proposal: ensure end-event is emitted from a best-effort fallback when transport signals closure during flush; add idempotent terminal marker to protocol so clients can detect completion even when trailing token set is partial.
2026-03-01 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer confirmed they can temporarily extend CDN keepalive to 120s as a mitigation while we test a runtime patch. They will monitor and report back.
2026-03-03 - Eng (Marco Rivera): Runtime changes landed on branch and test matrix passing. Preparing canary deployment to dedicated pool for verification.
resolution: Mitigation and fix in progress. Temporary workaround provided to customer: increase CDN keepalive to avoid mid-flush resets and enable client-side tolerant-finalization that treats partial terminal choice with explicit retry guard. A server-side patch to ensure an idempotent terminal marker is emitted on abrupt transport closure has been implemented and will be rolled out to canary pools on 2026-03-04.
resolution_notes: Workaround: Customer extended CDN keepalive to 120s; reduced incidents to <0.5% in their testing window.

Code fix: serving-runtime will emit a reserved 'terminal:forced' end marker on best-effort when transport closure is detected during tail flush. This avoids ambiguous missing-end cases and lets clients finalize deterministically.
Canary: Deploy to 5% of dedicated pools in us-east on 2026-03-04; monitor end-event vs abrupt-close metrics and error rates. Rollback plan prepared if we see increased partial duplication.

Follow-up: Create SDK guidance doc (confluence) recommending idempotent handlers for final-choice semantics and a sample backoff for dedupe. Ticket INT-418 created to track automatic detection/alerting for elevated 'abrupt-close without end-event' rates.
